title: Logachev Vladislav v Public Prosecutor
catchwords: Criminal law — Statutory offences — Casino cheating
body: The Court of Appeal considered sentencing for syndicated cheating at play in a casino. The offending was planned, transnational and involved the covert recording and transmission of cards. The court set out a sentencing framework that evaluates the harm caused and the offender's culpability. Relevant considerations include the amount involved, sophistication, duration, role in the syndicate and whether the offender acted for gain. The judgment discusses deterrence in offences that threaten confidence in regulated gambling operations. It also explains when an appellate court may intervene in sentence and how sentencing precedents should be used. The court emphasised that a framework guides rather than replaces the exercise of judgment on the facts of each case.
